@mi\_leeli Mi, a Change Request is the reviewable package. It contains one or more Operations; updating a record is one Operation with a starting version and a proposed change. That gives you a before/after diff and a history of who submitted it.

At merge time, Busabase compares the proposal with the current record. If Claude Code and Codex changed different fields, both changes can merge. If they changed the same field differently, the later merge reports a conflict instead of silently overwriting the first value; the proposal needs to be revised against the current record. A proposal-level connection waits for human review, while write access can merge a non-conflicting change immediately. [...] Hi, I'm Kelly from Busabase. We're building an open-source database and workspace where the records, docs, skills, and apps a team chooses to keep can be reused by people and connected AI agents.  
One problem we keep running into: an agent finishes useful work, but the result stays buried in a chat. The next person or agent has to reconstruct the project background and decisions before moving forward. In Busabase, that work can live in a shared workspace, with access controlled by permissions and review when needed.  
How does your team handle this today? Where do you keep the project context that multiple agents need, and what gets lost most often when you move between tools like Claude Code and Codex? I'd love to hear what's working for you and what still breaks.
